subject: Geography
topic: Peninsular drainage II — Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, Narmada, Tapti, Mahanadi
description: Peninsular rivers: Godavari (longest peninsular), Krishna (second longest), Kaveri (sacred, Karnataka/TN), Narmada and Tapti (west-flowing estuaries), Mahanadi (Hirakud Dam) — origin, tributaries, dams, economic significance.

questions.stem: The Godavari is called the 'Dakshina Ganga' (Ganga of the South). It is the longest peninsular river of India, originating from:

options.option_text: Trimbakeshwar, near Nashik, Maharashtra — flows ~1,465 km before joining the Bay of Bengal
Mahabaleshwar, Maharashtra — this is the origin of the Krishna River, not the Godavari
Talakaveri, Coorg, Karnataka — this is the origin of the Kaveri River, not the Godavari
Amarkantak, Madhya Pradesh — this is the origin of both the Narmada and Son rivers

questions.explanation: GODAVARI: longest peninsular river (~1,465 km). Origin: Trimbakeshwar (Brahmagiri hills, near Nashik, Maharashtra). Direction: W→E, drains into Bay of Bengal (Andhra Pradesh delta). States: Maharashtra, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Andhra Pradesh. MAJOR TRIBUTARIES: Pranhita (biggest; = Wardha + Wainganga + Penganga), Indravati, Sabari, Manjira. DELTA: forms a large fertile delta in AP (Rajamahendravaram area); important for rice cultivation. SACRED: Pushkaram festival (pilgrimage along Godavari) every 12 years. POLAVARAM PROJECT (Indira Sagar): multipurpose dam under construction in AP on Godavari — national project. ORIGIN COMPARISON: Nashik (Godavari) → NE Maharashtra; Mahabaleshwar (Krishna) → W Maharashtra; Talakaveri/Brahmagiri (Kaveri) → Karnataka; Amarkantak (Narmada) → MP. MEMORY: 'God-avari from God-Nashik' or 'G comes first in alphabet, G = longest (Godavari).' PYQ FREQUENCY: Godavari origin + length in SSC CGL, IBPS PO, RRB NTPC Geography GA — 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Unlike most peninsular rivers that flow eastward into the Bay of Bengal, the Narmada and Tapti (Tapi) rivers flow westward into the Arabian Sea because:

options.option_text: They flow through rift valleys (graben structures) between the Vindhya/Satpura ranges, not across the Deccan plateau
The Arabian Sea is lower in altitude than the Bay of Bengal, naturally pulling rivers westward
The Western Ghats create a water divide that prevents east-west flow for all rivers in this region
The Himalayas block the northern path, forcing these rivers to turn west instead of east either

questions.explanation: STRUCTURAL GEOLOGY: Narmada and Tapti flow through GRABENS (fault-bounded valleys, also called RIFT VALLEYS) between: NARMADA: flows between Vindhya range (north) and Satpura range (south). TAPTI: flows between Satpura range (north) and Ajanta/Mahadeo hills (south). RIFT VALLEY FORMATION: the land between two parallel faults dropped downward → river formed in this graben → the river's course was already set WESTWARD toward the sea by the rift's orientation. CONSEQUENCE: they do NOT form deltas (unlike east-flowing rivers) — they form ESTUARIES because they enter the sea steeply. SURAT (Tapti estuary) and BHARUCH/Bhadoch (Narmada estuary) are located at these estuaries. EAST-FLOWING RIVERS: flow across the Deccan plateau's gentle eastward slope → form deltas (sediment deposited). OTHER WEST-FLOWING: Mahi, Sabarmati, Luni (all in Gujarat/Rajasthan, for different topographic reasons). OPTION B is wrong: both seas are at sea level — elevation doesn't vary between oceans. PYQ FREQUENCY: Narmada-Tapti rift valley flow in SSC CGL, UPSC Prelims, RRB NTPC — 1-2× per cycle. A examiner favourite.

questions.stem: Hirakud Dam, one of the world's longest earthen dams, is built across which river?

options.option_text: Mahanadi — Hirakud Dam in Odisha (completed 1957, reservoir spans ~743 km²)
Godavari — the major multipurpose project on Godavari is the Polavaram/Indira Sagar Dam
Krishna — the major dams on Krishna are Nagarjuna Sagar and Srisailam Dam
Narmada — the major dam on Narmada is the Sardar Sarovar Dam (SSP) in Gujarat

questions.explanation: HIRAKUD DAM: built across the MAHANADI River at Sambalpur, Odisha. Completed 1957 — one of the first major multipurpose projects of independent India. LENGTH: ~25.8 km main dam + dykes = ~60 km total — one of the world's longest dams. RESERVOIR: Hirakud reservoir, ~743 km² area, ~316 km shoreline. MAHANADI RIVER: 858 km long, originates in Chhattisgarh (Sihawa hills, near Raipur), flows through Odisha into Bay of Bengal via a delta. 'Maha' = great, 'Nadi' = river. Odisha's major river. DAM COMPARISON TABLE: (1) HIRAKUD → Mahanadi (Odisha). (2) NAGARJUNA SAGAR → Krishna (Telangana/AP). (3) SRISAILAM → Krishna (Telangana/AP). (4) SARDAR SAROVAR → Narmada (Gujarat). (5) METTUR/STANLEY → Kaveri (Tamil Nadu). (6) POLAVARAM → Godavari (AP, under construction). (7) TUNGABHADRA → Tungabhadra (Karnataka/AP). PYQ FREQUENCY: Hirakud Dam river identification in SSC CGL, IBPS PO, RRB NTPC Geography — 1-2× per year.

questions.stem: The Kaveri (Cauvery) water dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu is one of India's oldest inter-state water conflicts. The Kaveri originates from:

options.option_text: Talakaveri, Brahmagiri hills, Coorg (Kodagu) district, Karnataka
Mahabaleshwar, Maharashtra — the origin of the Krishna, not the Kaveri
Trimbakeshwar, Nashik — the origin of the Godavari, not the Kaveri
Nilgiri hills, Tamil Nadu — the Kaveri flows through but does not originate in the Nilgiris

questions.explanation: KAVERI (CAUVERY): sacred river of South India; called 'Dakshina Ganga' by some (but Godavari also gets this title). LENGTH: ~800 km. ORIGIN: Talakaveri, Brahmagiri hills, Coorg (Kodagu), Karnataka. DIRECTION: flows SE through Karnataka → Tamil Nadu → Bay of Bengal (Kaveri delta near Thanjavur). SACRED: Kaveri Pushkaram; Srirangam island (formed by Kaveri and Kollidam channels). MAJOR TRIBUTARIES: Hemavati, Shimsha, Arkavathi (Karnataka), Bhavani, Amaravathi, Noyyal (Tamil Nadu). MAJOR DAMS: Krishnarajasagar (KRS) — Karnataka; Mettur (Stanley Reservoir) — Tamil Nadu; Kabini Dam — Karnataka. KAVERI WATER DISPUTE: the river flows through Karnataka first → Karnataka built dams → Tamil Nadu claims prior use rights (1892 agreement under British). Kaveri Water Disputes Tribunal (1990); Supreme Court final verdict allocating shares. CURRENT: Kaveri Water Management Authority (CWMA) under SC direction. PYQ FREQUENCY: Kaveri origin + dispute in SSC CGL, IBPS PO, UPSC GS-1 — 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: The Krishna River's major tributaries include the Tungabhadra, which is famous for being associated with:

options.option_text: Hampi (Vijayanagara Empire) — the ancient capital was situated on the Tungabhadra's banks
Ajanta Caves — the Ajanta Buddhist caves are on the Waghora River, not the Tungabhadra
Nalanda University — Nalanda is in Bihar, far from the Tungabhadra basin
Sanchi Stupa — Sanchi is in Madhya Pradesh on the banks of the Betwa, not Tungabhadra

questions.explanation: TUNGABHADRA RIVER: formed by the confluence of Tunga and Bhadra rivers at Koodli, Karnataka. Joins the Krishna at Kurnool (Andhra Pradesh). HAMPI (VIJAYANAGARA): the magnificent Vijayanagara Empire (14th-16th century) had its capital on the banks of the Tungabhadra. Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1986). The river served as a natural barrier and water source for this great empire. TUNGABHADRA DAM: at Hospet, Karnataka — important irrigation project for both Karnataka and AP. KRISHNA RIVER: second longest peninsular river (~1,400 km). Origin: Mahabaleshwar (Maharashtra). Flows through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, AP → Bay of Bengal. TRIBUTARIES OF KRISHNA: Tungabhadra (biggest), Bhima, Musi, Vedavathi. Nagarjuna Sagar: on Krishna in Telangana/AP — one of the largest masonry dams in the world; related to Nagarjunakonda (ancient Buddhist site near the reservoir). PYQ FREQUENCY: Tungabhadra-Hampi association in SSC CGL, UPSC GS-1 Art & Culture, IBPS PO — 1× per 2 years.

questions.stem: The Marble Rocks of Bhedaghat, a famous geological feature near Jabalpur, are carved through by:

options.option_text: The Narmada River — it flows through a 3 km narrow gorge of white marble/dolomite cliffs
The Son River — the Son also originates near Amarkantak but flows northeast, not through marble
The Betwa River — the Betwa flows through Madhya Pradesh but is associated with Orchha, not Bhedaghat
The Chambal River — the Chambal has ravines (beehads) but they are sandstone, not marble

questions.explanation: MARBLE ROCKS, BHEDAGHAT: a UNESCO tentative World Heritage Site near Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh. The NARMADA River cuts through ~3 km of white-and-grey crystalline dolomite/marble cliffs rising ~30 metres. DHUAN-DHAR FALLS: just upstream at Bhedaghat, Narmada drops spectacularly creating 'smoke' (dhuan) of mist. NARMADA RIVER KEY FACTS: Length ~1,312 km (5th longest in India). Origin: Amarkantak plateau, Anuppur district, MP (also origin of Son River — both from Amarkantak but flowing in opposite directions). Direction: W→E… actually WEST — flows W into Arabian Sea at Gulf of Khambhat/Cambay near Bharuch. States: MP, Maharashtra, Gujarat. NARMADA BACHAO ANDOLAN (NBA): led by Medha Patkar — agitation against Sardar Sarovar Dam displacement. SARDAR SAROVAR PROJECT (SSP): in Gujarat — height controversy; Supreme Court allowed completion in 2000. DINDORI, MANDLA, JABALPUR (Marble Rocks), BHARUCH (estuary) — major cities along Narmada. PYQ FREQUENCY: Marble Rocks + Narmada in SSC CGL, IBPS PO, UPSC GS-1 Geography — 1× per 2 years.

questions.stem: The Indravati River, a major right-bank tributary of the Godavari, is significant partly because the Chitrakote Waterfall (often called the 'Niagara of India') is located on it. Which state has the highest proportion of the Indravati basin within its territory?

options.option_text: Chhattisgarh — the Indravati flows through Bastar district, a biodiversity-rich forested plateau
Andhra Pradesh — the Indravati joins the Godavari in AP but most of its basin is elsewhere
Maharashtra — the Godavari basin is large in Maharashtra but the Indravati sub-basin is not
Telangana — the Godavari enters Telangana lower downstream; Indravati has joined it before

questions.explanation: INDRAVATI RIVER: a major right-bank tributary of the Godavari. Origin: Eastern Ghats (Kalahandi district, Odisha). Length: ~535 km. Basin: predominantly through CHHATTISGARH (Bastar division) and partly Odisha. CHITRAKOTE WATERFALL: on the Indravati near Jagdalpur, Bastar, Chhattisgarh. Width during monsoon: up to 300 m — broader than Niagara (though not as tall). Height: ~30 m. BASTAR SIGNIFICANCE: tribally rich region (Gond, Halba); dense forest; part of the Indravati National Park (now Indravati Tiger Reserve). NAXAL BELT: Bastar/Chhattisgarh-Odisha corridor is part of the 'Red Corridor' — context for UPSC GS-3 internal security. INDRAVATI NATIONAL PARK: one of the few remaining habitats of the endangered Wild Buffalo (Bubalus arnee) in India. GODAVARI TRIBUTARIES (right bank, flowing from south/west): Maner, Wardha-Wainganga (Pranhita), Sabari. GODAVARI TRIBUTARIES (left bank, flowing from north): Purna, Pranhita, Indravati. UPSC ANGLE: India's internal rivers and tribal geography are favourite UPSC GS-1 and state PSC geography topics. PYQ FREQUENCY: Indravati-Godavari system in UPSC Prelims, SSC CGL Geography GA — occasional but discriminating question.
